id: Practice Direction 74A – Enforcement Of Judgments In Different Jurisdictions
content:
# PRACTICE DIRECTION 74A – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS

# This Practice Direction supplements Part 74

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 74] Contents of this Practice Direction

## 1 This practice direction is divided into two sections –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 74 > 1 This practice direction is divided into two sections –] (1) Section I – Provisions about the enforcement of judgments

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 74 > 1 This practice direction is divided into two sections –] (2) Section II – The Merchant Shipping (Liner Conferences) Act 1982

## SECTION I ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS

## Meaning of ‘judgment’

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 74 > Meaning of ‘judgment’] 2 In rule 74.2(1)(c), the definition of ‘judgment’ is ‘subject to any other enactment’. Such provisions include –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 74 > Meaning of ‘judgment’] (1) section 9(1) of the 1920 Act, which limits enforcement under that Act to judgments of superior courts;

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 74 > Meaning of ‘judgment’] (2) section 1(1) of the 1933 Act, which limits enforcement under that Act to judgments of those courts specified in the relevant Order in Council;

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 74 > Meaning of ‘judgment’] (3) section 1(2) of the 1933 Act, which limits enforcement under that Act to money judgments;

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 74 > Meaning of ‘judgment’] (4) section 15 (1) of the 1982 Act, which limits enforcement under Part I of that Act to judgments within the meaning given by article 4(1) of the 2005 Hague Convention and article 3(1) of the 2019 Hague Convention.

## Registers

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 74 > Registers] 3 There will be kept in the Central Office of the Senior Courts at the Royal Courts of Justice, under the direction of the Senior Master –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 74 > Registers] (1) registers of foreign judgments ordered by the High Court to be enforced following applications under –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 74 > Registers] (a) section 9 of the 1920 Act;

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 74 > Registers] (b) section 2 of the 1933 Act;

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 74 > Registers] (c) sections 4, 4B and 4C of the 1982 Act;

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 74 > Registers] (d) (omitted)

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 74 > Registers] (2) registers of certificates issued for the enforcement in foreign countries of High Court judgments under the 1920, 1933 and 1982 Acts, and under article 13 of the 2005 Hague Convention, article 12 of the 2019 Hague Convention;

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 74 > Registers] (3) a register of certificates filed in the Central Office of the High Court under rule 74.15(2) for the enforcement of money judgments given by the courts of Scotland or Northern Ireland;

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 74 > Registers] (4) a register of certificates issued under rule 74.16(3) for the enforcement of non-money judgments given by the courts of Scotland or Northern Ireland;

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 74 > Registers] (5) registers of certificates issued under rules 74.17 and 74.18 for the enforcement of High Court judgments in Scotland or Northern Ireland under Schedule 6 or Schedule 7 to the 1982 Act.

## Registration of judgments for enforcement

## 4.1 Applications for –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 74 > 4.1 Applications for –] (1) foreign judgments under rule 74.3;

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 74 > 4.1 Applications for –] (2) judgments of courts in Scotland or Northern Ireland under rule 74.15 or 74.16;

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 74 > 4.1 Applications for –] are assigned to the King’s Bench Division and may be heard by a Master.

## Making an application

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 74 > Making an application] 4.2 An application under rule 74.12 for a certified copy of a High Court or county court judgment for enforcement abroad must be made –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 74 > Making an application] (1) in the case of a judgment given in the Chancery Division or the Kings Bench Division of the High Court, to a Master, Registrar or district judge;

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 74 > Making an application] (2) in the case of a judgment given in the Family Division of the High Court, to a district judge of that Division;

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 74 > Making an application] (3) in the case of a county court judgment, to a district judge, unless Practice Direction 2E applies.

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 74 > Making an application] 4.3 An application under rule 74.17 or 74.18 for a certificate or a certified copy of a High Court or county court judgment for enforcement in Scotland or Northern Ireland must be made –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 74 > Making an application] (1) in the case of a judgment given in the Chancery Division or the King’s Bench Division of the High Court, to a Master, Registrar or district judge;

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 74 > Making an application] (2) in the case of a judgment given in the Family Division of the High Court, to a district judge of that Division;

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 74 > Making an application] (3) in the case of a county court judgment, to a district judge, unless Practice Direction 2E applies.

## 4.4 The following applications must be made under Part 23 –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 74 > 4.4 The following applications must be made under Part 23 –] (1) applications under rule 74.3 for the registration of a judgment;

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 74 > 4.4 The following applications must be made under Part 23 –] (2) applications under rule 74.7 to set aside the registration of a judgment;

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 74 > 4.4 The following applications must be made under Part 23 –] (3) applications under rule 74.12 for a certified copy of a judgment;

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 74 > 4.4 The following applications must be made under Part 23 –] (4) applications under section III for a certificate for enforcement of a judgment;

## Applications under the 1920 Act or 1933 Act

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 74 > Applications under the 1920 Act or 1933 Act] 5 Foreign judgments are enforceable in England and Wales under the 1920 or 1933 Act where there is an agreement on the reciprocal enforcement of judgments between the United Kingdom and the country in which the judgment was given. Such an agreement may contain particular provisions governing the enforcement of judgments (for example limiting the categories of judgments which are enforceable, or the courts whose judgments are enforceable). Any such specific limitations will be listed in the Order in Council giving effect in the United Kingdom to the agreement in question, and the rules in Section I of P

## 6.1 to 6D.2 Omitted

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 74 > 6.1 to 6D.2 Omitted] 6E Evidence in support of an application under section 4B of the 1982 Act (Registration and enforcement of judgments under the 2005 Hague Convention).

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 74 > 6.1 to 6D.2 Omitted] 6E.1 Where a judgment is to be recognised or enforced in a Contracting State which is a State bound by the 2005 Hague Convention, that Convention applies.

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 74 > 6.1 to 6D.2 Omitted] 6E.2 The text of the 2005 Hague Convention is available at: https://www.hcch.net/ and Chapter III contains the provisions on recognition and enforcement.

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 74 > 6.1 to 6D.2 Omitted] 6E.3 Article 13 of the 2005 Hague Convention sets out the documents which need to be produced by a party seeking recognition or enforcement of a judgment.

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 74 > 6.1 to 6D.2 Omitted] 6E.4 The Civil Jurisdiction and Judgments (Hague Convention on Choice of Court Agreements 2005) Regulations 2015 (SI 2015/1644) make amendments to the Civil Jurisdiction and Judgments Act 1982 and the CPR in respect of the 2005 Hague Convention.

## Certified copies of judgments issued under rule 74.12

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 74 > Certified copies of judgments issued under rule 74.12] 7.1 In an application by a judgment creditor under rule 74.12 for the enforcement abroad of a High Court judgment, the certified copy of the judgment will be an office copy, and will be accompanied by a certificate signed by a judge. The judgment and certificate will be sealed with the Seal of the Senior Courts.

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 74 > Certified copies of judgments issued under rule 74.12] 7.2 In an application by a judgment creditor under rule 74.12 for the enforcement abroad of a County Court judgment, the certified copy will be a sealed copy, and will be accompanied by a certificate signed by a judge or, where Practice Direction 2E applies, a legal adviser.

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 74 > Certified copies of judgments issued under rule 74.12] 7.3 Subject to paragraph 7.6, in applications under the 1920, 1933 or 1982 Acts, the certificate will be in Form 110, and will have annexed to it a copy of the claim form by which the proceedings were begun.

## 7.4 and 7. 5 Omitted

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 74 > 7.4 and 7. 5 Omitted] 7.6 In an application under section 12 of the 1982 Act relating to recognition and enforcement of a judgment under the 2005 Hague Convention, the certificate will be in the form recommended and published by the Hague Conference on Private International Law and annexed to the final act of the twentieth session of the Hague Conference on Private International law, which is available at: http://www.hcch.net/ .

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 74 > 7.4 and 7. 5 Omitted] 7.7 In an application under section 12 of the 1982 Act relating to recognition and enforcement of a judgment under the 2019 Hague Convention, the certificate will be in the form recommended and published by the Hague Conference on Private International Law, which is available at: http://www.hcch.net/ .

## Certificates under section III of Part 74

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 74 > Certificates under section III of Part 74] 8.1 A certificate of a money judgment of a court in Scotland or Northern Ireland must be filed for enforcement under rule 74.15(2) in the Action Department of the Central Office of the Senior Courts, Royal Courts of Justice, Strand, London WC2A 2LL. The copy will be sealed by a court officer before being returned to the applicant.

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 74 > Certificates under section III of Part 74] 8.2 A certificate issued under rule 74.17 for the enforcement in Scotland or Northern Ireland of a money judgment of the High Court or of a county court will be in Form 111.

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 74 > Certificates under section III of Part 74] 8.3 In an application by a judgment creditor under rule 74.18 for the enforcement in Scotland or Northern Ireland of a non-money judgment of the High Court or of a county court, the certified copy of the judgment will be a sealed copy to which will be annexed a certificate in Form 112.

## Section II – Omitted
